beats.text: Two well-known agile methods: Extreme Programming, called X P, and Scrum.
X P works in weekly cycles. On the first day, the customer picks the stories for that week. By the end of the week, there are running, tested features. A quarterly cycle is a release.
X P writes the test first. Write a failing test. Run it and watch it fail. Write code until it passes. Run it again. Repeat. That is test-driven development.
All production code is pair programmed. The driver types. The navigator reviews every line.
Code is integrated many times a day, anyone may change any code, and the pace is sustainable: a forty-hour week.
Scrum starts with a backlog: the customer's wants and needs, each one a user story.
A sprint is a thirty-day cycle. It takes a set of stories from the backlog.
Every day, the scrum master runs the daily scrum. No more than fifteen minutes.
A scrum team has no more than six to nine members.
At the end of the sprint, the team shows the customer a demonstration of working, integrated, tested software.
